We need propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need to output JSON route with type mol root, children reaction nodes etc. Need to select appropriate template IDs. We need to find templates matching each step: likely step1: amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). In target, we have amide: C(=O)N attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: break amide to carboxylic acid and amine. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde? Actually amide from carboxylic acid + amine. So precursor1: acid: /C=C/C(=O) (the unsaturated acid) attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl? Wait structure: phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually there is an aniline attached to amide nitrogen (Nc3ccccc3N). So amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So amide formed from carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step1: break amide.

Step2: The unsaturated acid likely formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. The unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which is sulfonyl attached to another phenyl (with methyl). So the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring via para position? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has the unsaturated amide substituent. So Doebner modification would generate the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to that phenyl ring from aldehyde (the same phenyl ring with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So step2: break C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid.

Step3: Sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide linking the first phenyl (with methyl) to the second phenyl (c2). So break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride and amine? Typically sulfonamide formed from amine and sulfonyl chloride. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid?) and aniline (the phenyl with methyl). The sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride of p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl). So precursor: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl) and aniline (the second phenyl with the unsaturated amide). So step3: sulfonamide formation.

Thus route: target -> step1 (amide formation) -> precursors: unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then step2 (Doebner) on unsaturated acid -> aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid. Step3 (sulfonamide) on aniline? Wait sulfonamide is between first phenyl (with methyl) and second phenyl (the one bearing unsaturated acid). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (with methyl) as NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl. So the nitrogen is part of the first phenyl's substituent? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the methyl phenyl (p-tolyl) as N-SO2-aryl. So the sulfonamide formation step would involve p-toluidine (aniline with methyl) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). Actually typical sulfonamide: Ar-NH-SO2-Ar'. Here we have Ar (tolyl) attached to N, then SO2 attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break N-S bond to give p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (or aryl sulfonic acid). The aryl sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (c2) which also bears the unsaturated amide substituent. So step3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2SO2Cl). But we also need malonic acid as third component for Doebner? Actually Doebner uses malonic acid, but the unsaturated acid is product; retrosynthesis step2 would give aldehyde and malonic acid. So final set of starting materials: p-toluidine, aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2), malonic acid, and maybe also aniline (c3ccccc3N) as amine for amide step? Wait amide step uses aniline (c3ccccc3N) as nucleophile. So final starting materials: p-toluidine, aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2), malonic acid, aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's 4 building blocks, but route has 3 reactions, each reaction may involve two reactants. Reaction1 (amide) uses unsaturated acid and aniline. Reaction2 (Doebner) uses aldehyde and malonic acid to give unsaturated acid. Reaction3 (sulfonamide) uses p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (derived from aldehyde? Actually aryl sulfonyl chloride is derived from the same aromatic ring that after Doebner becomes unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the same aromatic ring that later gets unsaturated acid substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the same aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde? Actually after step3, we have aryl sulfonyl chloride attached to p-toluidine to give sulfonamide. Then step2 modifies that aryl ring (the one attached to sulfonamide) via Doebner to install unsaturated acid. So order: step3 (sulfonamide) first, then step2 (Doebner) on the aryl sulfonamide? But the guidance says reactions enumerated in order they must be applied forward. So forward order: 1) carboxylic acid to amide, 2) Doebner, 3) sulfonamide formation. So retrosynthetic order reverse: start from target, first break amide (step1), then break unsaturated acid to aldehyde+malonic (step2), then break sulfonamide to p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (step3). So final precursors: p-toluidine, aromatic aldehyde, malonic acid, aniline.

We need template IDs. We don't have them; we can search using search_template_catalog_by_criteria. Let's search for amide formation: functional_groups_broken: ["carboxylic_acid"], functional_groups_formed: ["amide"] maybe.
